issues.description: The problem statement/UML requires Ride to have a public constructor that takes both attributes (name: String, abbreviation: char) in that order. In the provided solution, Ride only has a constructor Ride(String name) which assigns a default abbreviation ('A'), while RollerCoaster and the launched subclasses call super(name, abbreviation). This creates a constructor signature mismatch (and a compile error) between Ride and its subclasses and contradicts the UML/constructor requirements, preventing students from implementing the intended inheritance/constructor chaining.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Ride constructor match the UML/spec: add a public constructor Ride(String name, char abbreviation) that assigns both attributes. Ensure subclasses call super(name, abbreviation). This aligns the implementation with the UML and removes the compilation/signature mismatch.
